speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; can you tell me how long you have had this and if you recall any new soaps, detergents, or plants you were exposed to recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the chronicity and lack of identifiable triggers make this complex. Have you noticed any specific patterns, such as the rash improving with sunlight exposure or occurring specifically on the backs of your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Polymorphous Light Eruption. The chronic, pruritic nature of your rash on the upper extremities, combined with the absence of systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain and no history of new allergens, strongly suggests a light-induced dermatosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the rash on the dorsal aspect of the hands. REQUEST TEST: Serum Vitamin D level.
